source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
Pursat orange grows best in a tropical climate with consistent access to water. It is planted in various regions of Cambodia, but does particularly well in areas with reliable irrigation, moderate rainfall, and good natural drainage - traditionally along riverbanks and in the lowland plains around Pursat province.

The crop is sensitive to waterlogging: land that floods or holds standing water for long periods is not suitable, since citrus roots are easily damaged by prolonged saturation. Farmers considering a new planting site should look for slightly elevated or well-drained ground, protected from strong wind and with year-round access to water for irrigation during the dry season.
